basics.name: Hayeon Jeong
basics.label: MS Student
basics.summary: I am an MS student in the Multimedia Computing & Machine Learning (MCML) group at Yonsei University, advised by Prof. Jong-Seok Lee, and a six-month Visiting Graduate Researcher at the Computational Machine Learning Lab, UCLA, advised by Prof. Cho-Jui Hsieh. My research interests span visual generative models, post-training for generative models, mechanistic interpretability, and AI safety & reliability.

research interests.name: Visual Generative Models
research interests.summary: Text-to-image diffusion: post-training, reward modeling, and evaluation.

research interests.name: Post-training for Generative Models
research interests.summary: RL and preference-based post-training to better align generative models with prompt requirements.

research interests.name: Mechanistic Interpretability
research interests.summary: Understanding the internal mechanisms (e.g., cross-attention) behind generative behavior.

research interests.name: AI Safety & Reliability
research interests.summary: Robustness, failure analysis, and trustworthy behavior in modern AI systems.

research experience.name: UCLA
highlights: Part of the CML Lab, advised by Prof. Cho-Jui Hsieh.

Working on Flip What Fails (first author): RL post-training of text-to-image models on long real-user prompts with counterfactual pairs that flip only the requirements a model fails, preserving satisfied ones.

research experience.name: Yonsei University
highlights: Part of the MCML Lab, advised by Prof. Jong-Seok Lee.

Formalized concept dominance in multi-concept diffusion generation and built DominanceBench; showed via controlled fine-tuning that low training-image diversity drives it, and found through head ablation that, unlike memorization, it cannot be removed by ablating any small set of heads (under review, ACCV '26).

research experience.name: Soongsil University
highlights: Part of the AI Safety Center, advised by Prof. Daeseon Choi.

Trained YOLOv5/YOLOv8 person detectors and ran the full physical-world experiment (printed patches, 20 participants, paired RGB–thermal capture) for a thermal-guided adversarial-patch defense (AVSS '25).
Built an on-device privacy assistant that summarizes consent forms with LLaMA-3 8B Instruct; key-phrase marking raised precision from 77.3% to 98.8% (Best Paper Award, KIISC Chungcheong Conference).

publications.name: Dominating vs. Dominated: Concept-Level Generative Collapse in Diffusion Models
publications.summary: We identify and analyze the Dominant-vs-Dominated (DvD) imbalance in text-to-image diffusion models, where one concept suppresses others in multi-concept generation. Through a systematic benchmark and attention-level analysis, we show that this behavior arises from limited data diversity and distributed cross-attention mechanisms, providing insights toward more reliable and controllable image generation.

publications.name: Infrared Thermal-Guided Adversarial Patch Defense for Robust Visible Person Detectors
publications.authors: Sohee Park, Hayeon Jeong, Daeseon Choi
publications.summary: We propose a defense against adversarial patch attacks on visible person detectors by leveraging infrared thermal information. By exploiting thermal differences between humans and adversarial patches, our method effectively detects and mitigates physical attacks while preserving performance on clean images.

projects.name: Phonetic-Aware Encoder Tuning for L2 Korean Speech Recognition
projects.summary: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) framework robust to phonetic disruption in non-native Korean speech via a LoRA-adapted Whisper encoder with auxiliary connectionist temporal classification (CTC) supervision.

projects.name: Border Conditions in Adversarial Patch Attacks (Undergraduate Thesis)
projects.summary: Showed on YOLOv5 that patch border color, thickness, and interpolation shift hiding-attack success rates by up to 9.8 points (4.5 on average); gray 4–8 px borders help most. 2nd Place, Undergraduate Thesis Competition, Soongsil University.

projects.name: Lightweight DenseNet
projects.summary: EMNIST classifier with a DenseNet variant using 10× fewer parameters than ResNet-50 and half the training time, and 2× faster than DenseNet-121. Team of 4 (team lead).
